text: In Descartes's substance dualism, what is the fundamental relationship between mind and body?
choices: Mental states are identical to brain-state types, just as water is identical to H₂O.
There is a single physical substance that nonetheless instantiates irreducibly mental properties.
Mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — an unextended thinking thing (res cogitans) and an extended, spatial thing (res extensa) — neither reducible to the other.
Mental states are defined by their causal roles, so what physically realizes them is irrelevant.
explanation: Substance dualism posits two distinct substances whose essential attributes, thought and extension, are incompatible, which is why Descartes concludes they are really distinct. Option 0 states the type-identity theory, option 1 states property dualism (one substance bearing irreducible mental properties), and option 3 states functionalism. Each is a genuine rival, but the signature of substance dualism is a plurality of substances, not merely of properties.
